title: Efim and Strange Grade
statementMd:
Efim just received his grade for the last test. He studies in a special school and his grade can be equal to any positive decimal fraction. First he got disappointed, as he expected a way more pleasant result. Then, he developed a tricky plan. Each second, he can ask his teacher to round the grade at any place after the decimal point (also, he can ask to round to the nearest integer).

There are $*t*$ seconds left till the end of the break, so Efim has to act fast. Help him find what is the maximum grade he can get in no more than $*t*$ seconds. Note, that he can choose to not use all $*t*$ seconds. Moreover, he can even choose to not round the grade at all.

In this problem, classic rounding rules are used: while rounding number to the $*n*$-th digit one has to take a look at the digit $*n* + 1$. If it is less than $5$ than the $*n*$-th digit remain unchanged while all subsequent digits are replaced with $0$. Otherwise, if the $*n* + 1$ digit is greater or equal to $5$, the digit at the position $*n*$ is increased by $1$ (this might also change some other digits, if this one was equal to $9$) and all subsequent digits are replaced with $0$. At the end, all trailing zeroes are thrown away.

For example, if the number $1.14$ is rounded to the first decimal place, the result is $1.1$, while if we round $1.5$ to the nearest integer, the result is $2$. Rounding number $1.299996121$ in the fifth decimal place will result in number $1.3$.

## Input

The first line of the input contains two integers $*n*$ and $*t*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 200 000$, $1 ≤ *t* ≤ 10^{9}$) — the length of Efim's grade and the number of seconds till the end of the break respectively.

The second line contains the grade itself. It's guaranteed that the grade is a positive number, containing at least one digit after the decimal points, and it's representation doesn't finish with $0$.

## Output

Print the maximum grade that Efim can get in $*t*$ seconds. Do not print trailing zeroes.

## Note

In the first two samples Efim initially has grade $10.245$.

During the first second Efim can obtain grade $10.25$, and then $10.3$ during the next second. Note, that the answer $10.30$ will be considered incorrect.

In the third sample the optimal strategy is to not perform any rounding at all.
statementZhMd:
Efim 刚刚得到了上次考试的成绩。他就读于一所特殊的学校，他的成绩可以是任意正十进制小数。起初他很失望，因为他原本期待一个更加令人愉快的结果。随后，他制定了一个巧妙的计划。每秒钟，他都可以请求老师将成绩在小数点后的任意位置进行四舍五入（也可以请求将其四舍五入到最接近的整数）。

距离课间休息结束还有 $*t*$ 秒，因此 Efim 必须抓紧时间。请帮助他求出在不超过 $*t*$ 秒的时间内，他能够得到的最高成绩。注意，他可以选择不使用全部 $*t*$ 秒。此外，他甚至可以选择完全不进行四舍五入。

本题使用经典的四舍五入规则：将数字四舍五入到第 $*n*$ 位时，需要查看第 $*n* + 1$ 位。如果它小于 $5$，则第 $*n*$ 位保持不变，其后的所有数字都替换为 $0$。否则，如果第 $*n* + 1$ 位大于或等于 $5$，则第 $*n*$ 位加 $1$（如果该位原本是 $9$，这可能还会改变其他位），其后的所有数字都替换为 $0$。最后，去掉所有末尾的零。

例如，将数字 $1.14$ 四舍五入到小数点后第一位，结果为 $1.1$；而将 $1.5$ 四舍五入到最接近的整数，结果为 $2$。将数字 $1.299996121$ 四舍五入到小数点后第五位，结果为 $1.3$。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*t*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 200 000$, $1 ≤ *t* ≤ 10^{9}$）——Efim 成绩的长度，以及距离课间休息结束的剩余秒数。

第二行包含成绩本身。保证该成绩是一个正数，且小数点后至少有一位数字，并且其表示形式不以 $0$ 结尾。

## 输出格式

输出 Efim 在 $*t*$ 秒内能够得到的最高成绩。不要输出末尾的零。

## 说明

在前两个样例中，Efim 最初的成绩为 $10.245$。

第一秒，Efim 可以将成绩变为 $10.25$；下一秒，他可以将成绩变为 $10.3$。注意，答案 $10.30$ 将被判定为错误。

在第三个样例中，最优策略是完全不进行任何四舍五入。
